 ## Breaking changes
 
 ### Thinking can’t be disabled
 
 On Claude Opus 5, thinking is on by default and `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` is accepted at effort `high` or below.
-On Claude Opus 5.5, thinking is always on: a request that sets `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}`, or a manual budget with `thinking: {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": N}`, returns a 400 `invalid_request_error`.

 Omit the `thinking` field, or send `thinking: {"type": "adaptive"}`, which is equivalent.

 ### Thinking blocks are tied to the model and the conversation
 
-Every thinking block records which model produced it, and each model reads its own blocks and only some other models’.
-Claude Opus 5.5 reads thinking blocks from Claude Opus 5 and from earlier Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku models.
-On the Claude API and Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed), it also reads blocks from Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5.
-It doesn’t read blocks from Claude Fable or Claude Mythos models.
-On the Claude API, Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 read thinking blocks from Claude Opus 5.5.
-So do Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 on the Claude API.
-On Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed), Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 read the same blocks as on the Claude API.
-No other model does.
-A conversation that moves from Claude Opus 5 onto Claude Opus 5.5, or from Claude Opus 5.5 up to Claude Fable 5.1 or Claude Mythos 5.1 on the Claude API, keeps its reasoning.
-So does one that moves from Claude Opus 5.5 up to Claude Fable 5.2 or Claude Mythos 5.2 on the Claude API.
-One that moves from Claude Opus 5.5 to any model other than those four runs the turns after the switch without the previous model’s reasoning.
-So does one that moves onto Claude Opus 5.5 from a Claude Fable or Claude Mythos model.
-When a request carries a block the target model can’t read, the API drops it before the model sees it: the request succeeds, and dropped blocks aren’t billed.
+Every thinking block records which model produced it. A conversation that switches models keeps its earlier reasoning only if the model that it switches to can read the earlier model’s thinking blocks:
+
+| Switch                                                                                                        | Keeps its reasoning                                                            |
+| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
+| To Claude Opus 5.5, from Claude Opus 5 or earlier, Claude Sonnet 5 or earlier, or Claude Haiku 4.5 or earlier | Yes                                                                            |
+| To Claude Opus 5.5, from Claude Sonnet 5.5 or Claude Haiku 5.5                                                | Yes, on the Claude API and Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed) only |
+| To Claude Opus 5.5, from a Claude Fable or Claude Mythos model                                                | No                                                                             |
+| From Claude Opus 5.5, to Claude Fable 5.2 or Claude Mythos 5.2                                                | Yes, on the Claude API and Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed) only |
+| From Claude Opus 5.5, to Claude Fable 5.1 or Claude Mythos 5.1                                                | Yes, on the Claude API only                                                    |
+| From Claude Opus 5.5, to any other model                                                                      | No                                                                             |
+
+When a request carries a block the target model can’t read, the API drops it before the model sees it.
+The request succeeds, and dropped blocks aren’t billed.
 With the `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` beta header, the drop is reported in a top-level `input_transformations` array.
 See [Switching models mid-conversation](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/preserved-thinking#switching-models).
+For switches that don’t involve Claude Opus 5.5, see [Which model switches keep the reasoning on the Claude API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/preserved-thinking#which-model-switches-keep-reasoning).
 
 The API also checks whether anything before a Claude Opus 5.5 thinking block (the `system` prompt, the `tools`, or an earlier message) has changed since the block was produced.
 Keep the conversation append-only: change instructions or tools with [mid-conversation system messages](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages) rather than edits.
-A request that replays a block after such a change and leaves `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior` unset gets a 400 error on accounts created on or after August 31, 2026, 00:00 UTC.
-This applies on the Claude API and on cloud platforms.
-On accounts created before that date, the request gets the error only when it sets the field to `"error"`.
+
+A request that replays a block after such a change, with `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior` unset, gets a 400 error.
+This applies to accounts created on or after August 31, 2026, 00:00 UTC.
+[Preserved thinking availability](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/preserved-thinking#feature-availability) lists the platforms where this applies.
+On accounts created before that date, the request might or might not get the error.
 To drop the affected blocks instead, send the `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` beta header and set the field to `"drop_block"`.
 See [Preserved thinking](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/preserved-thinking) and the migration guide’s [note on thinking blocks](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/opus-5-5/migration-guide#thinking-blocks).

 ## Feature support
 
-Claude Opus 5.5 supports [per-message effort](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort#change-effort-mid-conversation-beta) (beta), [mid-conversation system messages](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages), [task budgets](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/task-budgets), [prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching) with a 512-token minimum cacheable prompt, [batch processing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing), the [Files API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/files), [PDF support](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/pdf-support), [vision](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/vision), and server-side and client-side [tools](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview).
+Claude Opus 5.5 supports [per-message effort](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort-per-message) (in beta), [mid-conversation system messages](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages), [task budgets](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/task-budgets), [prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching) with a 512-token minimum cacheable prompt, [batch processing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing), the [Files API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/files), [PDF support](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/pdf-support), [vision](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/vision), and server-side and client-side tools (see [Tool use with Claude](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview)).
 See each feature’s page for model availability.
 
 ### Fast mode
 
 [Fast mode](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/fast-mode) is available for Claude Opus 5.5 on the Claude API, on [Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed)](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-models-on-google-cloud/anthropic-managed), and on [Claude in Microsoft Foundry](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry) for deployments hosted on Azure.
 On the Claude API and on Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed), set `speed: "fast"` on your request.
-Claude Opus 5.5 doesn’t need a beta header.
 See [Fast mode](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/fast-mode) for supported models, rate limits, and pricing.
 
 ### Define tools in a message (beta)
